column1: # Allowed callers of guarded kernel functions: GitHub issue #1107 (folds
# scripts/buildcheck_allowed_callers.py reads the --facts callgraph.tsv table of
# each kernel object and, for every row, refuses a function outside the
# allowed set that calls the guarded function or takes it as a value, and
# refuses a table in which an allowed caller no longer calls it.
# Columns (tab-separated): check name, guarded function, allowed callers as
# comma-separated file:function, issue, reason (printed on a refusal).
# Adding a caller is a review: write why it may name the function here.

column5: TPIDR_EL1 is read only by cpu_authority.tkb's preempt_slot_index(); any other caller is a second, unreviewed way to name the current CPU
the exec inode is stored only from a SyscallExecInode by syscall.tkb's syscall_exec_inode_store; any other caller would store an inode the format check never judged
dc civac is DDB-only: rp1_gem.tkb's kernel_net_rx_frame_pending() is its one reviewed caller; any other caller is cache maintenance outside the DMA owners

the QEMU virt (no bus offset) address of a DMA span is given only to a virtio-mmio queue or descriptor by these reviewed writers; a new caller is a new device-visible address, reviewed against dma_address.tkb's rule

the RP1 bus address of a DMA span is given only to a GEM or xHCI descriptor or register by these reviewed writers; a new caller is a new device-visible address, reviewed against dma_address.tkb's rule
a DMA span's CPU physical address is taken only for rp1_gem's DDB RX look (#959, #1095); any other caller is CPU access to a device region outside its owner
PSTATE.PAN is cleared only by the linear UserAccessWindow, whose closer is owed on every path; any other caller opens user memory to EL1 with nothing to close it
PSTATE.PAN is set again only by the window closer that consumes the UserAccessWindow

a user-access window is opened only by the user_memory.tkb accessors, each around one access to a range already validated (and its COW pages resolved); any other opener is an EL1 user access outside a checked range

an AddressSpaceRoot carries its backing handle, read once where it is made, so its makers are the authority-taking functions of process.tkb (run lock, owner, running evidence, full machine stop) and the backing's publisher, which wrote the handle it mints with; any other maker is a root whose handle no authority read

the whole-table free-list rebuild runs only where the runtime tables are installed; after that the list changes only by O(1) push and unlink, and a call from an allocation or release path costs about 3 ms under the IRQ-masking page lock on the RPi5 without failing a functional test

the entry mint reads the level from the frame SPSR, so it serves only the IRQ entries and return hooks handed a frame of either level, the exit path successor frame, and the debugger and crash reporter; any other caller makes a FrameRef from an address no entry handed over
the syscall entry frame, El0 by the vector it came through, or a boot probe stand-in; any other caller claims an El0 frame no such entry produced

a frame rebuilt from a process record saved_sp, indexed by that record owner: every delivery and scheduler pickup goes through scheduled_process_saved_frame; any other caller rebuilds a frame without the owner
a frame written whole before it is resumed, El0 by what is written: a clone child frame and PID 1 first frame (#831); any other caller claims a whole frame nobody wrote
the syscall dispatch entry is the one place a raw frame address may turn out to be no frame; any other caller is a new unreviewed entry

the stack-wide TCP retransmit pass runs on an interrupt return to EL0 and in the idle loop, never on a syscall return (maintainer, 2026-10-24), so a call in kernel_process_stack_switch_complete, which every syscall return runs, is refused
